analysis.title: Most Of The Santa Rally Comes After December 15: Goldman's "Chopsgiving" Seasonal Map Says Dip First, Gravy Later
key_insights: Goldman's Flow of Funds trio (Gail Hafif, Brian Garrett, Lee Coppersmith) says the Nov-Dec seasonal window has started but institutions have sold tech and cut leverage while retail has supported the market. Goldman calls it still a trader's market with violent day-to-day reversals and rotations.

Goldman's historical S&P path from Nov 16 to Dec 31 since 1928 dips about 0.5% into Nov 20, rises to about +1.1% by the first week of December, gives back about two-thirds into mid-December, then reaches about +2.4% by year-end. ZeroHedge's read of the chart is that about 80% of the average gain comes after Dec 14.

The Nasdaq 100 path since 1985 follows the same shape with larger moves: about a 1% dip before Thanksgiving, a roughly 4.5-point rise to early December, a roughly 1.5-point slide into mid-month, and a finish near +4.3%. These are ZeroHedge's approximate chart readings.

Since 1990, in the 17 years when VIX started mid-November at 18 or higher, VIX was lower by year-end in 14 of them, by 3.25 points on average. In those years SPX's mean year-end gain was +1.34% and it was up in 59% of years. The median drawdown within the window is -3.0%, and from Dec 15 to year-end the mean SPX gain is +1.22%, with SPX up in 27 of 36 years.

Retail net bought $6.19B of US equities last week, the largest weekly total of the 11 weeks since Sep 1. Retail's share of notional traded rose to 9.01% from 8.61% over Sep 1-Nov 6, and peaked at 10.0% on Nov 12. Buying was concentrated in semis and mega-cap tech, led by Nvidia (+$1.75B), AMD and Tesla (+$523M).
US-listed equity ETFs took in $59.3B last week, ahead of 91% of the 46 weeks so far this year. Fixed income ETF inflows fell to $2.6B from $13.7B, with outflows after the hot CPI.

Goldman says retail activity usually rises into Thanksgiving, dips during Thanksgiving week, picks up in mid-December and fades over the holidays. It warns that if this week's test (Nvidia's first print under interim CEO Colette Kress) disappoints or retail reduces buying, losing that support could drastically change the setup for US equities into year-end.

On Goldman's prime book, Info Tech was by far the most net sold global and US sector for another week. The US tech long/short ratio is 1.5, the lowest on record (since 2016), against a YTD peak of 2.14 in early June.

US fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 1.6 points to 209.1% (34th percentile, one-year) and net rose 2.1 points to 45.4% (4th percentile). US-listed ETF shorts fell 8.6%, the largest covering in seven months, and single stocks were heavily net sold (-1.7 standard deviations), mainly through short sales.

Semiconductor sector ETFs lost $7.3B last week, against an average weekly inflow of $6.2B over the prior four weeks. SOXL took in $5.10B in the week of Nov 5 and lost $4.17B the next week, its largest weekly outflow in a year. SOXS lost $4.38B over the two weeks and cut its share count by two-thirds. SOXX and SMH barely moved.
Goldman's Korea desk flagged a 5.3% SOX drop on Monday, which sent KOSPI futures down 1.8% overnight.

CTAs sold over $22B of S&P futures and almost $2.5B of Nasdaq futures over the past week, taking overall US equity positioning to short almost $10B, the lowest since April. Vol control and risk parity sold a combined $30B.

With vol off its highs, Goldman says CTAs are now buyers in a flat tape and flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks. Its one-week projection is a US$9.86B buy in a flat tape, a US$16.1B buy in an up tape and about a US$5.23B sell in a down tape. The one-month down-tape scenario is a sell of $122.97B ($20.31B US).

Buyback desk volumes are running 1.3x both 2025 and 2024 YTD ADTV, and about 94% of the S&P is in its open window. Goldman expects the window to stay open until Dec 13. 2026 YTD authorizations are $1.52T against $1.27T a year ago.
The GS Panic Index is at 6.3/10, and Goldman says the vol market has not turned off the seatbelt sign. It also flags thin holiday liquidity.

Goldman's bottom line is that equities will choppily grind moderately higher, with turbulence over the next two weeks. Systematic flows are skewed to the upside, and retail and corporates have defended their bid until the holidays. With institutional positioning light, a sustained move lower would likely need a move higher first.

ZeroHedge's own view, not Goldman's, is that the 3% median drawdown looks more likely than a Thanksgiving ramp. It sees the bid from retail, buybacks (window closing Dec 13) and conditional systematic buying as vulnerable to Nvidia's first post-Jensen print, a Fed hike priced at 113% and holiday liquidity. It expects any real Santa rally after Dec 15.

market_movers.rationale: Retail bought $1.75B of Nvidia last week, and Morgan Stanley estimated $1.6B of retail NVDA buying on Thursday alone. The first Nvidia print under interim CEO Colette Kress is this week's test for retail support.
AMD was among the leading retail net purchases last week, with the extracted text garbling the dollar amount.
Retail net bought about $523M of Tesla last week, among the largest single-name purchases.

sector_views.rationale: Institutions on Goldman's prime book net sold Info Tech more than any other sector for another week, and the US tech long/short ratio is a record low of 1.5.
Sector ETFs saw $7.3B of outflows last week, and levered semis ETFs swung sharply between large inflows and outflows, which Goldman reads as lack of conviction.

earnings_insights: Nvidia's first print under interim CEO Colette Kress is described as this week's test for retail support. The article gives no EPS or revenue estimates for it, and the print had not occurred as of the article date, Nov 18, 2026.

A hot CPI print preceded the sell-off in stocks and bonds and fixed income ETF outflows. No numeric value is given.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman expects equities to grind moderately higher. Systematic flows are skewed to the upside for the first time in weeks, retail and corporates have defended their bid, and positioning is light, with hedge funds at the 4th percentile of net leverage and CTAs net short.
tension_points.bear_case: ZeroHedge argues the bid depends on retail (which seasonally fades and is nervous ahead of Nvidia's print), on buybacks (window closes Dec 13) and on machines that buy only if nothing breaks. It expects the 3% median drawdown to come before any real Santa rally after Dec 15.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A disappointing Nvidia print this week or reduced retail buying, which Goldman says could drastically change the setup for US equities into year-end.
